tools.name: arobi_authorize
tools.description: Decide whether an agent action is permitted against a sealed route grant, and seal an AUTHORIZATION record in your ledger. Returns GRANTED, DENIED or ESCALATED with the reason; a GRANTED decision also carries an authorization_seal, which a consumer that spends the authorization must present back. Ca

tools.name: arobi_route_grant
tools.description: Seal WHO granted WHAT authority to WHICH workflow, with scope, caps, attenuation and expiry, as a ROUTE_GRANT record in your ledger. One grant authorises many later arobi_authorize decisions. The grant is made by the tenant your key belongs to, and it must expire. To end one early, use arobi_revoke_

tools.name: arobi_revoke_grant
tools.description: End a route grant before it expires: seal a ROUTE_REVOKE record chained to the grant. Pass the route_revoke it returns to arobi_authorize, and the grant authorizes nothing more. Only the tenant that made the grant can revoke it.

tools.name: arobi_classify_and_route
tools.description: Classify a prompt and choose the cheapest route CAPABLE of the work from your candidate set, reporting whether any cost above the cheapest capable route is justified by a named required capability, by measured quality under your explicit quality_exception policy (one task class) or escalation policy

tools.name: arobi_verify_chain
tools.description: Recompute a set of sealed spine records and report whether the hash chain is continuous, which record breaks it, and why. Verification only — it re-derives, it does not re-execute, and it writes nothing.

tools.name: arobi_list_records
tools.description: List the sealed records of your own workspace, newest first: each record's id, kind, digest (its SHA-256 hash), when it was sealed and its block in the Arobi ledger. Digests and kinds only, never a record's content. One call is one count against your key, whatever it returns. It does not verify anyt
